sentences.text: Niobrarasaurus coleii is the sole species within this extinct genus, representing an armored dinosaur roughly 5 meters long, 1.8 meters high, and weighing between 227 and 453 kilograms.
However, a higher estimate by Paul suggests the animal reached 6.5 meters in length and weighed 4 tons.
As a nodosaurid ankylosaurian, this creature lacked the club on its tail found in some relatives.
Fossil evidence reveals possible shark bite marks on juvenile leg bones, indicating dangerous encounters in the water.
The genus name Niobrarasaurus was chosen to honor the Niobrara Formation where the fossils were found.
The remains were discovered in Gove County, about 11 miles south of Hackberry, Kansas, approximately 195 feet above the base of the Niobrara Formation.
In 2002, the type specimen was transferred to the Sternberg Museum of Natural History in Hays, Kansas.
Niobrarasaurus is classified within the family Nodosauridae, with the genus authority listed as Carpenter et al., 1995 and the species authority as Mehl, 1936.

The dinosaur lived at the end of the Cretaceous period, between 87 and 83 million years ago, during the Coniacian and Santonian stages, while the fossil record indicates a time range from the Coniacian to Santonian stages, between 89.8 and 83.6 million years ago.
The habitat was near the middle of the Western Interior Seaway during the Late Cretaceous.
It is debated whether Hierosaurus coleii should be considered a distinct genus or a synonym of Nodosaurus, leading to its reclassification as Niobrarasaurus.
